query: What distinct aspects of food quality do reviewers focus on?

per_column.name: taste_quality
per_column.rationale: Taste is a core constitutive sensory aspect of food quality -- a genuine part-of relationship.

per_column.name: flavor_authenticity
per_column.rationale: Whether flavor is true-to-type is an aspect of food quality, but it substantially overlaps with taste_quality since both concern the flavor/taste dimension.

per_column.name: functional_performance
per_column.rationale: Whether the product 'works as described' captures product performance/efficacy, not a constitutive aspect of food quality itself; it is external to the sensory/quality concept.

per_column.name: palatability_acceptance
per_column.rationale: Acceptance/refusal (eagerly accepted, refused) measures a reaction or outcome driven by quality, not a facet OF quality itself. It is a consequence, not a constitutive part.

judge.rationale: Only two of four columns are genuine facets of food quality (taste_quality, flavor_authenticity), and those two overlap heavily as both concern flavor/taste, lowering mutual exclusivity. functional_performance is product efficacy (external predictor) and palatability_acceptance is an acceptance outcome/reaction (consequence), neither being constitutive parts of the concept. The facet set also omits major constitutive aspects of food quality such as texture/mouthfeel, freshness, appearance, and aroma, so exhaustiveness is low.
